summary: Each generator advance must produce one value and can update the two-value recurrence state in constant time, matching the per-yield lower bound.

optimality.argument: Every call to next must return one yielded number and therefore requires Omega(1) work. The generator yields the stored previous value and performs one addition plus a constant-size state update, giving O(1) time per advance.

replacement_checks.evidence: Producing the required yielded value on one generator advance takes at least constant work.
Each advance performs one yield, one addition, and one two-variable reassignment regardless of the number of earlier calls.
Authored cases independently verify zero, one, and two advances, longer recurrence prefixes, persistent state, and the maximum fifty-call prefix.
